verdicts.quote: Method readBytes() allocates a byte array with size read directly from untrusted protocol input. Line 88: `byte [] buffer = new byte[(int)contentLength];` where contentLength is read from DataInputStream at line 86 and can be up to Integer.MAX_VALUE-1 (2,147,483,646 bytes = ~2 GB).
verdicts.why: This is the allocation-from-untrusted-length mechanism: the declared length drives new byte[...] up front, so a small message claiming a huge length gets the buffer allocated before the payload bytes are shown to exist.

verdicts.quote: No nesting depth limit or recursion check is implemented. A table containing a table containing a table... (arbitrarily deep) will recurse without bounds.
verdicts.why: F01 is exactly the mutual-recursion cycle: readFieldValue -> readTable/readArray -> readFieldValue with no depth counter, so input nesting controls depth.
